# --- 2. The direct route and GITHUB_TOKEN --------------------------------------
#
# Every asset comes from the direct browser route and no GitHub API request
# is made (ADR-0585) — the anonymous API's shared-IP rate limit is the
# failure this shape removes. GITHUB_TOKEN is not read at all.

reset_case
install_run token-unset
tap_check "token unset: installer exits 0" "$RUN_STATUS"
! grep -q "Authorization" "$RUN_LOG"
tap_check "token unset: no Authorization header in any curl call" $?
[ "$(direct_call_count)" -eq 3 ]
tap_check "token unset: exactly three direct downloads (manifest + signature + binary)" $?

reset_case
GITHUB_TOKEN=test-token
install_run token-set
tap_check "token set: installer exits 0 — the token is not read" "$RUN_STATUS"
! grep -q "Authorization" "$RUN_LOG"
tap_check "token set: no Authorization header anywhere (GITHUB_TOKEN never rides a request)" $?
assert_installed "token set: installs the fixture binary" "$fixtures/relate-darwin-arm64"

content.text:
The patch violates ADR-0585. I didn't run the test suite. The conclusion comes from reading the ADR references and the test file.

`distribution/install.sh` now sends `Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN` whenever the variable is set. `scripts/tests/test_install_sh.sh` states the rule: every asset comes from the direct release route, and `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not read at all. The "token set" test sets `GITHUB_TOKEN=test-token` and asserts that no Authorization header appears in any curl call. This patch would add one, so that assertion would fail.

I didn't open ADR-0585's file. I took its number and content from the test file's comment, so the ADR-0585 citation rests on that comment alone. The older ADRs (0068 and 0069) describe the earlier behaviour, where the token was sent. The test's comment points to ADR-0585 as the later rule.
